entries.subject: Chandra X-ray Center: MACS J0025.4-1222 (2008) in layers
entries.finding: Optical, X-ray and lensing each alone, TIFFs of 4200 x 4143 px on one frame. Their embedded sky tags give half the true scale: the optical layer was registered against Gaia DR3 (7 of 8 stars in the frame, 0.09 arcsec rms; 0.04666 arcsec per pixel, north 31.97 degrees right of vertical).

entries.subject: Depth of the gas and the mass
entries.finding: Nothing measures depth in the cluster. Bradač et al. (2008) give one gas peak and two total-mass peaks, a line-of-sight velocity difference of 100 +/- 80 km/s between the subclusters, and take the collision as head-on in the plane of the sky. The gas and the mass are each taken apart as a body of revolution about the line through the two mass peaks, drawn in the plane of the sky.

entries.subject: NOX star removal on the optical layer
entries.finding: NOX over macs_optical.tif, then again over a copy a quarter of the size for the saturated stars (7.76% of the picture took that pass). NOX takes compact light whatever it is, the cluster's galaxies with the Milky Way's stars, as on the Bullet Cluster's and El Gordo's pictures.
entries.revisitWhen: The cluster's galaxies are to come back: as dots at catalogued places, or by removing only the Gaia stars the frame was registered with.
